observations: A used automotive air conditioning compressor sits on a concrete floor.
It has a pulley with clutch, two service ports with caps, and a metal hose attached.
The body is cast aluminum with visible grime and surface rust near ports.
A watermark across the center reads partially as 'COOLING VENTURES'.
No brand name, model number, or part number is legible on the compressor in the photo.

claims.claim: Engine loose compressor for ford edge 2010 models
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a compressor but no readable part number or vehicle fitment marking; seller text alone cannot confirm fitment.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical condition: compressor may be seized, worn, or damaged internally.
risks.proof: Video of the pulley and clutch rotating freely by hand, or a bench test showing it pumps.

risks.risk: Fitment: it may not match a Ford Edge 2010 despite the seller's claim.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of a legible part number or OEM label on the compressor body.
risks.if_unproven: as unknown fitment, may not fit

risks.risk: Refrigerant or oil leaks: service ports may be open or contaminated.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of both service ports sealed and dry with no oily residue.

proof_requests: Close-up of any stamped part number or label on the compressor body.
Video showing the pulley and clutch turning freely.
Close-up of the service ports to confirm they are capped and dry.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a used car air conditioning compressor from the photo; the seller's Ford Edge fitment claim is unverified, so it is priced as a non-working compressor of unknown fitment.
